content:
A trig equation almost never has one answer. It has a whole family, wrapped up in that little n. Miss the general form, and you lose an easy mark. Try the free JEE Trigonometric Equations online test below. It gives 15 solved MCQs with instant scoring. Target 12 correct.

What JEE asks from trigonometric equations

  • Principal solutions inside 0 to 2 pi.
  • General solutions with the n term for sin, cos and tan.
  • Equations of the form a sin x plus b cos x equals c.
  • Quadratics in sin x or cos x, so factor first.
  • Bound checks that rule out impossible values.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Set sin x = sin a to x = n pi + (−1)^n a.
  • Solve cos x = cos a with x = 2 n pi ± a.
  • Solve tan x = tan a with x = n pi + a.
  • Keep a sin x plus b cos x within root of a squared plus b squared.
  • Reject any solution that makes a function undefined.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Cancelling sin x, and so losing the x = n pi roots.
  • Writing only the principal value, not the general one.
  • Missing that a sin x plus b cos x has a fixed maximum.
  • Squaring the equation, then keeping extra false roots.

quiz.title: JEE Trigonometric Equations Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The principal solutions of sin x = √3/2 are:
questions.explanation: sin x is positive in the first and second quadrants. So x = π/3 and x = π − π/3 = 2π/3.

questions.q: Solve 2cos²x + 3cos x + 1 = 0 for the general solution (n ∈ Z).
questions.explanation: Factor to (2cos x + 1)(cos x + 1) = 0. So cos x = −1/2 or −1, giving x = 2nπ ± 2π/3 or (2n+1)π.

questions.q: The principal solutions of cos x = −1/2 are:
questions.explanation: cos x is negative in the second and third quadrants. So the solutions are 2π/3 and 4π/3.

questions.q: The equation 9 sin x + 40 cos x = 43 has:
questions.explanation: The expression ranges from −41 to 41 since √(81+1600) = 41. As 43 > 41, no solution exists.

questions.q: The principal solutions of tan x = −1/√3 are:
questions.explanation: tan x is negative in the second and fourth quadrants. So x = 5π/6 and 11π/6.
Replace cos²x with 1 − sin²x. This gives 4sin²x + 4sin x − 3 = 0, so sin x = 1/2 and x = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/6).

questions.q: The principal solutions of cosec x = −2 are:
questions.explanation: cosec x = −2 means sin x = −1/2. The values in the third and fourth quadrants are 7π/6 and 11π/6.

questions.q: The equation 7 sin x + 24 cos x = 28 has:
questions.explanation: The range is −25 to 25 since √(49+576) = 25. As 28 > 25, no solution exists.

questions.q: The principal solutions of sec x = √2 are:
questions.explanation: sec x = √2 gives cos x = 1/√2, positive in the first and fourth quadrants. So x = π/4 and 7π/4.

questions.q: The principal solutions of cot x = 1 are:
questions.explanation: cot x = 1 means tan x = 1, positive in the first and third quadrants. So x = π/4 and 5π/4.

questions.q: The general solution of sin 2x = 0 is (n ∈ Z):
questions.explanation: sin θ = 0 gives θ = nπ. So 2x = nπ, which means x = nπ/2.

questions.q: Solve sin x tan x − 1 = tan x − sin x in [0, 2π).
questions.explanation: Factor to (tan x + 1)(sin x − 1) = 0. Reject sin x = 1 since tan x is undefined there, so tan x = −1 gives 3π/4 and 7π/4.

questions.q: The general solution of cos(x/2) = 0 is (n ∈ Z):
questions.explanation: cos θ = 0 gives θ = (2n+1)π/2. So x/2 = (2n+1)π/2, which means x = (2n+1)π.

questions.q: The general solution of tan 3x = 0 is (n ∈ Z):
questions.explanation: tan θ = 0 gives θ = nπ. So 3x = nπ, which means x = nπ/3.

questions.q: The general solution of sin x = 1/2 is (n ∈ Z):
questions.explanation: sin x = sin(π/6). The rule sin x = sin a gives x = nπ + (−1)ⁿa, so x = nπ + (−1)ⁿ(π/6).
